To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) in FEP, a 2- to3-year period of low-dose maintenance treatment is more effective than dose reduction/discontinuation for preventing relapse, 2) the risk of relapse is highest during the first 3 to 5 years after diagnosis, and 3) a low-dose maintenance strategy is associated with a significantly greater likelihood of functional recovery than dose reduction/discontinuous.

(1) patients who are in remission from psychosis can safely be randomized to DR or MT, (2) DR patients have twice the rate of functional recovery, (3) DR patients have no increased relapse rate at 7-year follow-up, and (4) the DR group used antipsychotic medication less frequently than the MT group.

1) the best predictor of functional recovery at the end of the study period was random assignment to dose reduction/discontinuation; and2) random assignment to dose-reduction/discontinuation had no adverse effect on the rate of relapses.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a model for the prevention of relapse and the promotion of recovery in FEP that can be applied to clinical practice.
the question, “What is the best way to use antipsychotic medication to maximize recovery?”
the development and testing of a new model of care, which we call the Recovery After Early Psychosis program, or REAP.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, in FEP, DR is not recommended for the first 3years after diagnosis, but after that time, it is an acceptable strategy.
the best use of antipsycotic medication for relapse prevention is a matter of timing.
the best way to maximize functional recovery in FEP is to use low doses of antipsychotics, as needed, for the first 3 to 5 years after remission.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the best outcomes are achieved by the earliest possible use of antipsy-chotic medications, with the lowest possible doses and the least possible exposure to side effects, and the most possible attention to psychosocial care.
the best outcomes are achieved by a careful and individualized balance of the benefits and risks of antipsychotics.
“less is more” in the critical period for FEP.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the goal of early intervention for FEP should not be relapse prevention, but functional recovery.
the first 3 to 5 years of FEP are the critical period for functional recovery.
the goal in FEP should be to pursue as complete a functional recovery aspossible, not just remission of symptoms.
